explanation.plain: geNorm's stepwise ranking keeps ALUsq(Eurogentec) and HPRT1 as the most stable and drops UBC(2) first. None of the candidates reaches geNorm's usual stability cut-off, so which control genes to use is a judgement call. With the recommended set versus UBC(2) alone: BIRC5 4× vs 5.2×, NM23A 2.2× vs 2.8×, NTRK1 0.066× vs 0.091× and ODC1 3.3× vs 4.1×. 31 genes out of 58 change their conclusion with this choice alone, so a person makes it. Even between sets of three or more control genes, 17 of 58 change. The control genes are not neutral here: the ratio HMBS:UBC(2) itself differs 1.8× between the groups (p = 0.058), and 3 of 10 pairs differ by at least 1.4×.

explanation.plain: Which wells count as amplified is a choice. LinRegPCR's own call counts a well when it finds a starting quantity; a Cq cut-off calls every well with a later Cq not detected, for every gene including the control genes. This analysis uses LinRegPCR's own call (a starting quantity was found), under which 323 study wells have no value. Changing only this choice: with Cq ≤ 35 (common, not recommended), 10 of 58 genes change their conclusion (1,642 study wells without a value); with Cq ≤ 38 (a later Cq counts as not detected), 3 of 58 genes change their conclusion (663 study wells without a value); with Cq ≤ 40 (a later Cq counts as not detected), 1 of 58 genes change their conclusion (460 study wells without a value). 11 genes out of 58 change their conclusion with this choice alone, so a person makes it.
